ports.note: Takes a point layer of cases, each with a date, and gives back the clusters it reports as circles: one polygon per cluster, carrying its days, places, observed and expected cases, likelihood ratio and p-value.

ontology.note: GAP, meaning no mapping to an external vocabulary. fw:SpaceTimeScan and fw:ScanCluster are declared in ontology/runtime.ttl with their properties. The receipt names the date column, the unit, the study period, every record not scanned and why, the limits, the replications, the seed and the random stream, and every cluster reported with its counts and p-value.

changes.description: The replay plays on the map (the practitioner, 2026-11-10: "Where do I see the day by day play"): its layer carries a timeline of days, and an interactive Map plays through them, drawing each day's most likely cluster and the cases with a date up to that day, with what the scan said that day in words. Hagelloch's cluster workflow has the map.

evidence.note: tests/space-time-scan.test.mjs (7 unit checks, the replay and the note among them) and tests/hagelloch-cluster-example.browser.mjs on Chromium, which checks both progress bars, the replay's first flagged day and the reference in References. Lab check 46: the retrospective scan recomputed in numpy; the replay is checked there too (see parity). 0.3.0: tests/hagelloch-cluster-example.browser.mjs plays to 21 November 1861 and finds 32 cases drawn and the day's p = 0.041 in the caption; Chromium.
